allowed_supporting_statements: The exact marginal decoder is a correctness oracle and approximation benchmark, not the practical flagship.
The present evidence supports a search-coordinate advantage for early and middle one-slip QPSK events.
Orbit screening is required; very-high-rate low-redundancy codes are not unrestricted targets.
Any practical advantage must survive optimized event-triggered state-aware baselines and a defensible physical model.

novelty_qualifier: To the best of our knowledge after the frozen scientific search, the identical combination of sparse intra-packet persistent automorphism-component ordering, arbitrary-code membership, adaptive first-valid/L=2 operation, and explicit orbit screening was not found. This is a provisional scientific novelty position, not a patent-validity or freedom-to-operate opinion.
primary_claim: For a frozen zero-or-one persistent QPSK phase-jump model, we study a code-agnostic latent-cause guessing receiver that globally orders state-conditioned candidate components and invokes an arbitrary code-membership oracle. The practical modes are first-valid decoding and an adaptively invoked two-codeword list with complete state-marginal rescoring. We measure actual noisy rank compression, tail work, and affine orbit safety against matched state-aware receivers.
working_title: Sparse Latent-Cause Guessing for Rare Persistent QPSK Phase-State Jumps
